# Instruments: external VSTi (third-party virtual instruments)

Use a VST3 / CLAP / LV2 instrument plugin installed on this machine as the sound source:

```json
{
  "name": "lead",
  "instrument": "plugin:/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT.clap",
  "instrument_params": { "A Filter 1 Type": "LP 24 dB", "A Filter 1 Cutoff": "800 Hz", "A Osc 1 Retrigger": "On" },
  "automation": [
    { "target": "instrument", "param": "A Filter 1 Cutoff", "shape": "points", "points": [[0, "200 Hz"], [16, "4000 Hz"]] }
  ],
  "clips": [ ... ]
}
```

- Syntax: `plugin:<absolute path>`; when the file contains several plugins use `plugin:<path>#<plugin id>` (`muser plugin scan` gives this form directly).
- `instrument_params` uses the plugin parameter **names** as keys (case-insensitive; a numeric id also works); the value is the text the plugin displays (`"800 Hz"`, `"LP 24 dB"`),
  a number (plugin automation scale: the declared range for CLAP/LV2, 0-1 for VST3), or true/false. When a name is wrong, similar parameter names are suggested.
- Parameters can be automated, written the same way as for built-in instruments, with the plugin parameter name in `param`.
- A plugin with a profile accepts short aliases (such as `"cutoff"`) and `"@preset": "<preset>"`; the profile's `setup` is applied automatically (`"@setup": false` turns it off);
  `"@state": "<file>"` loads a complete sound saved by `muser plugin save-state`. See [plugins.md](../plugins.md).
- A note's `pitch` is a MIDI pitch; the plugin decides the timbre and range itself. `accent` has no effect on plugins.
- `muser validate` loads the plugin to check parameter names and values; when rendering, the plugin is activated at the project's sample rate.
- Loading a plugin runs third-party code; use only trusted plugins on this machine.

How to get to know an unfamiliar plugin: see [plugins.md](../plugins.md).
- Plugin instruments receive the sustain pedal (CC64): the clip's `pedal` field, see [pedal.md](../pedal.md).
